summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.
summary.overview: Management reported operating revenue of Rs.167 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs.47 crore (+3%, margin 28.12%) for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs.172 crore (+10%) and EBITDA of Rs.52 crore (+8%). Occupancy held at 92%, but ADR growth was only about 2% amid West Asia disruption, weak international air traffic and flat domestic air traffic. PAT declined about 14% to close to Rs.12 crore, reflecting about Rs.2.5 crore higher finance charges from Zillion acquisition financing and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision on the move to the new tax regime. Management guided to a stronger ADR trend from Q2 onward, with the BRICS Summit, weddings and exhibitions cited as drivers.

segments.name: Food and Beverage
segments.commentary: F&B contributed about 43% of total revenue in Q1; Flurys stood at 111 outlets (cafes, kiosks, tea rooms) after adding one at Inorbit Mall Vizag, with first standalone North India cafe opened in Gurugram in August.

segments.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
segments.commentary: Portfolio stated as 42 hotels with 2,677 keys (one slide reference in call says 2,667). Ran Baas Patiala ARR about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace Chettinad about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata mixed-use project
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; expected cash inflow Rs.70-80 crore this year, of which Rs.21 crore received.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth guided to high single digits for the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show Bengaluru and Bharat Mobility Expo.
Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 from 2,677 keys.
Flurys target of 29 additional outlets in FY27, taking count to about 140; target of 400 outlets by 2030.
Long-term ambition of more than 6,000 keys by FY2030; management also cited 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Other income guided at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter; further cash inflow of about Rs.50 crore expected from EM Bypass by year-end.
Effective tax rate guided to fall to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under the new regime (from about 40% in Q1).
capex_capacity: EM Bypass Kolkata: 218 hotel rooms plus 69 service apartments, completion targeted early 2030; second Kolkata hotel referenced for opening in 2030.
The Park Juhu (78 rooms, converted from service apartments): design complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for Zillion acquisition.
Vizag 100-room hotel: on site, launch expected in August 2026, completion early 2030.
Malabar House, Fort Kochi (17 keys, about half an acre): acquisition in progress, completion expected October-November 2026; acquisition cost about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI raised from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan of 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential.

Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years: about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus Zillion acquisition about Rs.210 crore, Juhu renovation about Rs.80 crore and Kochi about Rs.64 crore (total about Rs.350 crore additional, cited with EM Bypass funding offset). Operating capex Rs.40 crore per year plus Flurys Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore per year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex expected within FY27.
Completed SAP S/4HANA implementation for Finance during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; RevPAR leadership in upper upscale maintained.

Management said All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter, versus about 2% for the company as stated in analyst question; domestic passenger traffic flat and international inbound air traffic down about 10%.
City-level domestic passenger declines cited: Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%.
Juhu ARR about Rs.18,000-20,000; management expects Bombay ARR growth of 10-15%.
Management expects ADR to improve from Q2 onward; said Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.
Pricing on EM Bypass service apartments: average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; Juhu acquisition at about Rs.40,000 per sq ft versus market levels cited near Rs.1 lakh per sq ft.

financial_highlights.value: close to Rs.12 crore; PAT margin close to 7%
Rs.4.79 crore, of which about Rs.2.7 crore from mutual funds

qa_highlights.question: Given 92% occupancy, how should ADR evolve and what long-term ADR growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADR pressure came from West Asia disruption, flat domestic passenger traffic and about 10% decline in international inbound traffic. All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter; it expects Q2-Q4 to be distinctly better and high single-digit ARR growth in the coming season, helped by BRICS Summit, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show and Bharat Mobility Expo.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Flurys still at 111 outlets versus aggressive plans, and how will the 29 additions be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Flurys has grown at a 21.5% CAGR since 2019 (17 outlets); five outlets opened so far with the rest mapped, including 3 Pune, 3 Mumbai, 5 Hyderabad, about 7 Delhi NCR, 4 Bengaluru and up to 10 PVR outlets under negotiation, targeting about 140 by year-end and 400 by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.4.79 crore other income run-rate sustainable over the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of Rs.4.79 crore included about Rs.2.7 crore from mutual funds; management guided Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter. About Rs.50 crore more EM Bypass cash is expected by year-end, to be added to mutual funds of about Rs.97 crore, so other income may rise.

qa_highlights.question: How mature is the existing portfolio and how long does stabilisation take for new hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Ran Baas (ARR about Rs.33,000) and Lotus Palace Chettinad (about Rs.13,000) are entering maturity, with occupancy stabilising over the year; a 15-room Vembanad Lake property acquired this year is expected to stabilise with its Q3-Q4 season. Typical stabilisation is 2-3 years, but high-potential markets like Mumbai and Pune are expected to stabilise in 1-1.5 years or the first year.

qa_highlights.question: How does the EM Bypass service apartment model change return on capital and land evaluation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model could lift RoCE from about 9-10% toward 20%+ as the project goes live, with cash flows of about Rs.70 crore this year, Rs.120 crore next year, Rs.100 crore in year three and Rs.30-40 crore in year four; sales of Rs.300-325 crore are meant to fund the hotel build, which management described as virtually free.

qa_highlights.question: What is the updated capex guidance for FY27 and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years is about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus about Rs.350 crore of Zillion, Juhu, Kochi and related items; net capex about Rs.1,500 crore against EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore a year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex falls within FY27, and Juhu's long-term financing is tied up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall 14% when revenue rose 8%, and what is the tax outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance charges rose about Rs.2.5 crore YoY mainly on Zillion acquisition financing, and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision came from moving to the new regime. Q1 tax was about Rs.8.71 crore at roughly 40%; the effective rate is guided to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4, and management asked that PAT be compared with Q4 rather than Q1.

risks_watch: ADR recovery in Q2-Q4 depends on the BRICS Summit, wedding season and exhibitions; Q1 ADR growth was only about 2% for the company versus 6% for the market.
International inbound air traffic fell about 10% and city-level domestic traffic declined (Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%), so West Asia and air-connectivity pressure could persist.
Finance costs will rise with Zillion acquisition debt and capex of about Rs.1,500 crore net over 4-5 years; FY27 capex of Rs.200-250 crore must be funded from EBITDA and EM Bypass cash.

Execution risk on the EM Bypass sales (Rs.70-80 crore this year, Rs.21 crore received), the Juhu conversion (78 rooms, October 2027), Vizag launch in August 2026 and the Kochi acquisition (October-November 2026).
Flurys needs 29 net additions in FY27 to reach about 140 outlets; progress against the 400-outlet 2030 target and the Adani, DLF, Phoenix and PVR tie-ups still unconfirmed.

Tax rate step-down to 30-35% from about 40% is guided but not yet visible; the PAT trend depends on it. Mutual fund holdings (about Rs.97 crore) were questioned for being regular rather than direct plans, and an investor's request for the fund list was not answered on the call.
key_quotes: So, we expect that the quarters ahead are going to be distinctly better than the quarter which has gone by.

This decline is due to the impact of higher finance costs to propel expansion during this period as well as deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores as the company shifts to the new favorable income tax regime.
And I would also request that if you are comparing PAT compare with the Q4 not to the tax rate with the Q4 not to the Q1.
So, we can expect definitely high single digit ARR growth as we go forward.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term outlook, expansion pipeline and EM Bypass cash flows, but cautious on near-term ADR, citing West Asia disruption and weak air traffic. It was defensive on the PAT decline, attributing it to finance costs and the tax-regime shift, and asked analysts to compare with Q4 rather than Q1.
